facts.text: Middletown was platted in 1829, just a few years after the first settlers arrived in the area.
The town officially became incorporated in 1840, giving it a formal municipal structure that still guides its governance today.
Middletown earned its name because it sits roughly halfway between New Castle and Anderson, a fact noted by early maps.
The Middletown‑Fall Creek Township Historical Society, founded in 1996, preserves local heritage through a museum and community programs.
Inside that museum, visitors can see artifacts, documents, and photographs that chronicle the town’s rich historical narrative.
Hedrick House and the Middletown Commercial Historic District are listed on the National Register of Historic Places, highlighting the town’s architectural legacy.
